description: AT&T is among the world’s largest telecommunications companies, offering wireless communications, broadband internet, and entertainment services. The company held a decades-long telephone monopoly in the U.S. before a 1982 antitrust settlement broke it into parts. In 2023, AT&T was the world’s largest telecommunications company by revenue. In 2022, AT&T finished merging its spinoff WarnerMedia with Discovery, a reorganization that resulted in the creation of Warner Bros. Discovery.

rankings.itemDescription:
AT&T falls 17 spots on this year’s list. The decline largely reflects the company’s 2021 divestiture of its Time Warner and DirectTV media and entertainment businesses; overall, revenue in 2022 was down 10% from the previous year.

  • AT&T was able to draw more customers to its wireless phone business in 2022 with the help of discounts and trade-ins. In the last three months of 2022, AT&T added more than 650,000 subscribers to one of the most lucrative parts of its business—postpaid phone ervice—outdoing some of its rivals.

  • The company increased prices on its wireless plans in June 2022 to cope with inflationary pressures.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Having acquired Time Warner and DirecTV in an attempt to become a major media player, AT&T spent much of 2021 dealing with the fact that the attempt had ultimately failed. It sold off its underperforming media businesses, merging them into a new company, Warner Bros. Discovery, while reaping some $40 billion in cash to help reduce its debt load. Overall, AT&T shed 28,000 employees over the course of 2021, as well as 14.5% of its share price. Despite the setbacks, AT&T’s core businesses fared well: Its fiber internet service ranked No. 1 in customer satisfaction in 2021 based on an American Customer Satisfaction Index survey. AT&T added 3.2 million phone subscribers in 2021, a tally that exceeded its net new customers gained in the previous 10 years combined. AT&T is now focused on growing its 5G network and fiber-optic footprint.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: AT&T CEO Randall Stephenson spent 13 years in command of the company, building a wireless and telecom giant and then acquiring DirecTV and Time Warner. But in June 2020 Stephenson retired, and his longtime lieutenant, John Stankey, took over. Stankey immediately faced plummeting revenue from the company’s movie production unit owing to cinemas being closed during the pandemic. Initially, that made it easier for him to shift new movie releases to AT&T’s HBO Max streaming service, which added 7 million new U.S. subscribers in 2020 thanks to the arrival of blockbusters like Wonder Woman 1984 and hit shows like The Flight Attendant. Still, needing more money to fund AT&T’s costly expansion into 5G wireless, Stankey sold 30% of DirecTV to private equity firm TPG, raising $8 billion. And in May 2021, the company announced its plans to spin off its WarnerMedia assets and merge them with Discovery—a stunning strategic about-face that represents an almost complete withdrawal from the “content” business.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Revenue at the newly created communications and entertainment conglomerate increased 6%, but profits dropped 28% amid merger costs, pension charges, and changes in the value of some assets, among other items. CEO Randall Stephenson, in what would turn out to be his last year at the helm, focused on breaking down barriers in the company's WarnerMedia unit and creating a streaming video strategy to attract cord cutters. Now it will be up to new CEO John Stankey, who took over July 1, to keep all the pieces working in harmony—from an expensive new 5G wireless network to newly launched streaming service HBO Max.
